s1.syndrome_frame: Hypertension with multisystem involvement and vascular abnormalities
salient_findings: Continuous murmur in the epigastric region
High-grade ostial stenosis of the left renal, celiac trunk, and superior mesenteric arteries
key_facts: Medical history includes bone and central diabetes insipidus
Liver involvement was treated with cytarabine for one year
Untreated dyslipidemia with LDL cholesterol 3.11 mmol/L
Transthoracic echocardiogram shows left ventricular mass index of 110 g/m²
Abdominal CT angiogram shows right kidney atrophy and high-grade ostial stenosis of multiple arteries

raw.syndrome_frame: Hypertension with multisystem involvement and vascular abnormalities
salient_findings: Continuous murmur in the epigastric region
High-grade ostial stenosis of the left renal, celiac trunk, and superior mesenteric arteries
key_facts: Medical history includes bone and central diabetes insipidus
Liver involvement was treated with cytarabine for one year
Untreated dyslipidemia with LDL cholesterol 3.11 mmol/L
Transthoracic echocardiogram shows left ventricular mass index of 110 g/m²
Abdominal CT angiogram shows right kidney atrophy and high-grade ostial stenosis of multiple arteries

differentials: Primary angiitis of the central nervous system
Langerhans cell histiocytosis with vascular involvement
per_call: Primary angiitis of the central nervous system
Langerhans cell histiocytosis with vascular involvement

shortlist.label: Takayasu arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: High-grade ostial stenosis of multiple arteries, including renal, celiac trunk, and superior mesenteric arteries, is consistent with large vessel vasculitis

shortlist.label: Fibromuscular dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Right kidney atrophy and high-grade ostial stenosis of renal artery are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Polyarteritis nodosa
shortlist.why_kept: Multisystem involvement, including hypertension, kidney atrophy, and vascular abnormalities, could be explained by this medium vessel vasculitis

shortlist.label: Atherosclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Untreated dyslipidemia and high blood pressure increase the risk of atherosclerotic disease, which could contribute to the patient's vascular abnormalities

shortlist.label: Moyamoya disease
shortlist.why_kept: High-grade ostial stenosis of multiple arteries and presence of difficult-to-treat hypertension could be related to this rare cerebrovascular disease

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of difficult-to-treat hypertension, high-grade ostial stenosis of multiple arteries (including the left renal, celiac trunk, and superior mesenteric arteries) as seen on the abdominal CT angiogram, and the absence of atherosclerotic risk factors (such as smoking or diabetes) are key findings that support Takayasu arteritis. Additionally, the patient's age and the involvement of multiple large arteries are consistent with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Fibromuscular dysplasia
rejected.why: While fibromuscular dysplasia can cause hypertension and renal artery stenosis, it typically affects medium and small-sized arteries and is less likely to cause the high-grade ostial stenosis of multiple large arteries seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Polyarteritis nodosa
rejected.why: Polyarteritis nodosa is a vasculitis that typically affects smaller arteries and is often associated with systemic symptoms and inflammatory markers, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Atherosclerosis
rejected.why: Atherosclerosis is unlikely given the patient's low body mass index, lack of smoking history, and absence of other atherosclerotic risk factors, as well as the pattern of arterial involvement.

rejected.label: Moyamoya disease
rejected.why: Moyamoya disease primarily affects the intracranial arteries and is not consistent with the pattern of arterial stenosis seen in this patient, which involves large arteries in the abdominal region.
